topic.title: What $1 billion really looks like in $100 bills

title: What $1 billion looks like in $100 bills 💵
description:
How big is a billion dollars, really?
From one $100 bill to a room full of pallets, level by level, and how far a whole $50,000-a-year career gets you, computed.
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before making financial decisions.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Guess how many briefcases a billion is? Comment

lines.text: Four levels to get there, each one bigger than the last. And the final one needs a forklift.
Level one. Band a stack of those notes together, and that's $10,000. It fits in my pocket.
Level two is $1 million. Strap after strap, packed into one briefcase. You could carry it in one hand.
One briefcase? On a salary of $50,000, saving every cent, that takes 20 years!
Level three is $100 million. Briefcase after briefcase, stacked onto one pallet, wrapped in plastic.
Way too heavy to carry. You'd need a forklift just to move it.
Level four, $1 billion. Pallet after pallet, until they fill a whole room.
Hold on. A billion is just one room? That doesn't sound so big.
Here's the part that hurts. Saving my whole salary for 40 years, I'd never even leave level two.
A whole career is a couple of briefcases. A billion is the whole room.
And that whole room? It's only one note, piled up.

Physical scale claims are accurate: a $10,000 strap is 100 $100 notes (pocket-sized), $1M is ~10 kg and fits one briefcase, $100M is ~1 tonne on one standard pallet (forklift needed), $1B is 10 pallets (a room). Description ends with the disclaimer. Style note: description lacks the profile's 'speak to a licensed financial adviser' line, and the on-screen '20000 years' could read '20,000'.
